name: Social anxiety disorder
summary: Marked fear of social or performance situations with avoidance and impairment. FDA-labeled options are paroxetine (IR/CR), sertraline, and venlafaxine ER. No new SAD drug was approved in 2024–2026; the intranasal fasedienol program missed its primary endpoint in two Phase 3 trials (PALISADE-3, Dec 2025; PALISADE-4, Jun 2026).
plainSummary: Social anxiety disorder is a strong, lasting fear of being judged or embarrassed around other people, which leads to avoiding social situations. CBT and daily medicines can help.

approved.indication: Treatment of social anxiety disorder (SAD) in adults.

dosing.start: IR: 20 mg once daily; CR: 12.5 mg once daily
dosing.target: IR: 20 mg/day (no clear added benefit above 20 mg); CR: titrate by 12.5 mg/day weekly
dosing.notes: IR: after 1–2 weeks may increase by 10 mg/day weekly. Geriatric, severe renal or hepatic impairment: IR start 10 mg, max 40 mg/day; CR start 12.5 mg, max 37.5 mg/day. Taper to stop.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
Drugs that prolong the QTc interval and are CYP2D6 substrates (e.g., thioridazine, pimozide)
approved.plainSummary: Paroxetine is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for social anxiety disorder in adults. Stopping it suddenly can cause withdrawal-like symptoms.

verified.note: Paxil CR SAD dosing confirmed on the Paxil CR label (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=483bd97f-c4d0-4e23-aaa8-6334f4471e0c). Approval year is for Paxil IR (1999); Paxil CR SAD approved 2003.

dosing.start: 25 mg once daily for 1 week, then 50 mg
dosing.notes: Increase by 25–50 mg/day once weekly. Mild hepatic impairment: half the usual dose; not recommended in moderate or severe impairment.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Sertraline is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for social anxiety disorder in adults.

approved.indication: Treatment of Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD), also known as Social Phobia, in adults.

dosing.max: 75 mg/day (no evidence of added benefit at higher doses)
dosing.notes: Take with food. Hepatic impairment: reduce dose by 50% or more. Renal impairment: reduce 25–50% (50% or more in severe impairment/dialysis). Monitor blood pressure.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Venlafaxine XR is a once-daily antidepressant (SNRI) approved for social anxiety disorder in adults.

verified.note: Venlafaxine ER tablets label (MDD and SAD only) also checked: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=38431a76-6185-4c17-994f-8278b6cd7510. Effexor XR SAD approval year from Drugs@FDA supplement dates (Feb 2003).

offLabel.notes: NICE first-line SSRI (with sertraline) for adults with SAD; not FDA-labeled for SAD. Usual SSRI cautions; Cochrane review supports SSRIs as a class.

references.label: Williams et al. 2017, Cochrane: Pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder

offLabel.use: SAD after non-response to a first SSRI
offLabel.notes: NICE alternative SSRI. Luvox CR held an FDA SAD indication (2008), but Luvox CR is discontinued and current generic fluvoxamine ER labels list OCD only, so SAD is off-label. Strong CYP1A2/2C19 inhibitor with many interactions (contraindicated with tizanidine, thioridazine, pimozide, alosetron, ramelteon).

references.label: Williams et al. 2017, Cochrane: Pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder

offLabel.notes: NICE option after non-response to an alternative SSRI or SNRI. Requires a tyramine-restricted diet and strict interaction precautions (serotonergic drugs, sympathomimetics); risk of hypertensive crisis and orthostasis.

references.label: Williams et al. 2017, Cochrane: Pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder

offLabel.notes: Some positive RCTs, but evidence is limited and NICE advises against routinely offering anticonvulsants for SAD. Cautions: sedation, dizziness, misuse potential, respiratory depression with opioids, renal dosing.

references.label: Williams et al. 2017, Cochrane: Pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder

offLabel.notes: Limited RCT support; NICE advises against routinely offering benzodiazepines for SAD. Boxed warnings: opioid co-use, misuse and addiction, dependence and withdrawal.

references.label: Williams et al. 2017, Cochrane: Pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder
